claude-opus-5|DUSP4.answer:
Strong promoter H3K4me3 is a hallmark of active/permissive chromatin and correlates with transcription in most cases, so I would expect DUSP4 to be at least moderately-to-highly expressed in K562 (with the caveat that H3K4me3 can also mark poised or bivalent promoters, so it is not by itself proof of high output).

expressed

claude-opus-5|NR4A3.answer:
Because NR4A3 is a serum/stimulus-responsive immediate‑early nuclear receptor whose promoter is typically kept H3K4me3‑marked and poised (often with paused Pol II) even when basal transcription is low, the presence of strong H3K4me3 in unstimulated K562 cells indicates a permissive promoter but does not by itself predict robust steady‑state expression.

uncertain

claude-opus-5|DEPTOR.answer:
Strong, broad H3K4me3 at a promoter is one of the most reliable chromatin correlates of active transcription, so I would expect DEPTOR to be transcribed in K562 (barring a bivalent H3K27me3-marked, poised state), likely at low-to-moderate rather than extreme levels.

expressed
